A failed run, one marked holding, and no recorded trade today

Paper trading · 2026-10-20T17:00:05.457383-04:00

This report uses records through 2026-10-20 21:00:05 UTC (5:00 p.m. EDT). The scheduled 19:15 UTC run failed while validating asset data. The only supplied holding is 0.053191 shares of MU in the mean-reversion book. Its value uses a bid/ask midpoint observed at 20:00 UTC (4:00 p.m. EDT), so this after-hours report uses a last-session observation, not a live price. Other reported cash and equity figures are book snapshots; missing holdings, performance, or reasoning remain unknown.

Today's lesson: Follow the evidence through each step

A proposal, a risk decision, an order submission, and a fill are separate events. Today's run failed during asset validation, so the records establish no completed proposal or deterministic risk approval or rejection. They also show no submitted order or fill. A submitted order alone would not prove a trade happened.

Portfolio review

The paper account snapshot at 2026-10-20 21:00:05 UTC showed $2,000 cash, $2,000 buying power, and $2,000 equity. No paper holding or same-day performance record is included in the supplied context. The scheduled run failed at 19:15 UTC while validating asset data, so it does not show a completed proposal or deterministic risk decision. No submitted order or broker or simulated fill is recorded for today. This is a failed run, not evidence of deliberate waiting.

What the run failure establishes

The failed run listed five asset validation errors for the exchange value TXSE. That explains why the run is marked failed, but it does not tell us what a completed book evaluation might have proposed or what deterministic risk would have decided. No broker fill or simulated fill for today appears in the supplied records.

What to watch next

Check whether the next recorded run completes, then compare its proposal, deterministic risk result, submitted orders, and actual fills as separate records. Note the observation time beside any quoted price.

Bid/ask midpoint: A recorded estimate based on the bid and ask, here the midpoint of those two quoted prices. It is tied to the observation time and may not be a live or closing-price feed.

Unrealized P&L: The estimated gain or loss on a holding that has not been closed. Here, MU's supplied value is about $2.02 below its recorded purchase basis, before fees.

Failed run: A record that the run did not complete. It does not establish that the system intentionally waited or that an attempted proposal was a completed decision.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
